topic.audience: r/LocalLLaMA readers running local language models
topic.scenario_status: Hypothetical experiment brief; not measured results or personal experience. State that status explicitly. Do not invent external facts or benchmarks.

facts.text: The hypothetical setup uses a 16 GB GPU.
The slowdown begins when context length changes from 2048 to 8192.
Model and runtime versions are not yet recorded.
No evidence proves a driver, memory or model issue.

draft.title: Hypothetical Slowdown: 16GB GPU, Context Length Increase (2048 -> 8192)
draft.body: I'm investigating a hypothetical performance issue in a local LLM setup. The scenario involves a 16 GB GPU. A noticeable slowdown is observed specifically when increasing the context length from 2048 tokens to 8192 tokens. The model and runtime versions are currently unrecorded, and there's no existing evidence pointing towards a driver, VRAM, or model-specific problem. This is purely a hypothetical experimental brief. My primary question is: what are the most probable causes for such a context length-dependent slowdown on a 16 GB GPU, assuming no other obvious hardware or software faults? Are there specific architectural features or common implementation bottlenecks that tend to manifest under these conditions? I'm looking for insights into potential areas to investigate in a real-world scenario, given these constraints.
draft.plan: Focus on architectural limitations and common bottlenecks related to context window expansion on limited VRAM. Avoid speculative solutions. Invite discussion on typical trade-offs.

The question is focused and invites discussion on architectural and implementation bottlenecks related to context length increase on a 16 GB GPU, which is relevant and useful for troubleshooting. The post is credible and not clickbait.

draft.title: Troubleshooting Hypothetical LLM Latency Jump with Increased Context on 16GB GPU
draft.body: This post outlines a hypothetical troubleshooting scenario for a local LLM. We're working with a setup featuring a 16 GB GPU. The core observation is a significant performance degradation when the context length is expanded from 2048 to 8192 tokens. It's important to note that this is a hypothetical experimental brief; model/runtime versions are not yet recorded, and there is currently no evidence implicating drivers, system memory, or the model weights themselves. The question is: what factors commonly contribute to such a pronounced latency increase when scaling context length on a system with a 16 GB VRAM constraint? Are there specific memory management strategies, attention mechanism variations, or quantization effects that might be disproportionately impacted by this change? Understanding these potential bottlenecks is key for future debugging efforts.
draft.plan: Explore potential causes related to memory bandwidth, attention computation scaling, and KV cache management under VRAM constraints. Keep discussion focused on the hypothetical nature and technical factors.
